questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is one-twentieth of their LCM. If one of the numbers is 96 and the difference of the LCM and the HCF is 456, then what is the other number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let HCF = 1 unit and LCM = 20 units.

Difference between LCM and HCF = 20 − 1 = 19 units.

Given 19 units = 456 ⇒ 1 unit (HCF) = 24.

LCM = 20 × 24 = 480.

Other Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number = (24 × 480) ÷ 96 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (n₁) = 96

HCF = LCM ÷ 20

LCM − HCF = 456

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2df10b69cfc840a9c0ccfad4073681e2cdb281fef1269ce04e706b53af84b3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let LCM = L and HCF = H.

⇒ H = L ÷ 20 ⇒ L = 20H.

⇒ L − H = 456

⇒ 20H − H = 456

⇒ 19H = 456

⇒ H = 456 ÷ 19 = 24.

⇒ L = 20 × 24 = 480.

⇒ Let the other number be n₂.

⇒ n₁ × n₂ = H × L

⇒ 96 × n₂ = 24 × 480

⇒ n₂ = (24 × 480) ÷ 96

⇒ n₂ = 480 ÷ 4 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule

For any two numbers a and b, the relationship is always: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Divisibility Property

The HCF of any set of numbers is always a factor of their LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their HCF is 1 and their LCM is equal to their product.</p

questions.question: The sum of the ages of Arun and Bharti is 24 years such that Arun is older. If the age of Arun and Bharti is doubled, the difference is 8 years. What is the age of Arun, in years?

Sum of ages (Arun + Bharti) = 24 years.

Difference of double of their ages = 8 years.

Current age difference (Arun − Bharti) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 years.

Arun is older, so Arun's age = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2.

Arun's age = (24 + 4) ÷ 2 = 14 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

questions.question: What is the correct descending order of the following ratios? (17)/(30),(7)/(15), (27)/(50),(11)/(20)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given fractions into percentages for a quick and direct comparison.

17/30 ≈ 56.67% and 7/15 ≈ 46.67%

27/50 = 54% and 11/20 = 55%

Arranging percentages in descending order: 56.67% > 55% > 54% > 46.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 17/30 > 11/20 > 27/50 > 7/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fractions: 17/30, 7/15, 27/50, 11/20

**Method Used:**

Find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all denominators to convert them into equivalent fractions with a common base.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The denominators are 30, 15, 50, and 20.

⇒ LCM of (30, 15, 50, 20) = 300

⇒ Convert 17/30: (17 × 10) ÷ (30 × 10) = 170/300

⇒ Convert 7/15: (7 × 20) ÷ (15 × 20) = 140/300

⇒ Convert 27/50: (27 × 6) ÷ (50 × 6) = 162/300

⇒ Convert 11/20: (11 × 15) ÷ (20 × 15) = 165/300

⇒ Comparing the numerators: 170 > 165 > 162 > 140

**∴ The correct answer is 17/30 > 11/20 > 27/50 > 7/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

To quickly compare two fractions a/b and c/d, cross multiply. If a × d > b × c, then a/b > c/d.

Multiplying a fraction by 100 converts it into a percentage, making multi-fraction comparisons visually straightforward.

A proper fraction always has a value less than 1 (Numerator < Denominator), while an improper fraction has a value equal to or greater than 1.

questions.question: In what ratio should rice costing Rs. 67.5 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 60 per kg to get an average price of Rs. 64 per kg?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By using the direct alligation cross-multiplication rule:

Quantity Ratio = (Mean Price − Cheaper Price) : (Dearer Price − Mean Price)

⇒ Ratio = (64 − 60) : (67.5 − 64)

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 3.5

⇒ Ratio = 8 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of first rice type = ₹67.5 per kg

Price of second rice type = ₹60 per kg

Average mean price = ₹64 per kg

**Formula Used:**

If two types of items of price p₁ and p₂ are mixed to get an average mean price pₘ, the ratio of their quantities q₁ : q₂ is (pₘ − p₂) : (p₁ − pₘ).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dc0edeeb4c3f17e84f4a6bda98684239a2f7ce22e7d075e6ea6eeff243a9ff3.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the required ratio be x : y.

⇒ Quantity ratio = (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper) : (Price of Dearer − Mean Price)

⇒ x : y = (64 − 60) : (67.5 − 64)

⇒ x : y = 4 : 3.5

Multiply both sides by 2 to convert into integer ratio:

⇒ x : y = 8 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 7.**

questions.question: A cube of side 5 cm, has been assembled using 125 cubes each of 1 cm edge. One cube is removed from the middle of each of the faces of the cube. What is the surface area (in cm²) of the remaining solid?

Surface area of a cube = 6(side)²

⇒ 4 × (1 cm)² = 4 cm²

Total increase in surface area after removing one cube from each face of the larger cube = 6 × (increase in area)

⇒ 6 × 4 cm² = 24 cm²

The overall surface area of the remaining shape is = original surface area + Total increase in surface area

150 cm2 + 24 cm2 = 174 cm2.

Which of the following statements about enzymes in the human body is/are correct?

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Maltase **is an** enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of maltose to simple sugar glucose.**
 
• This is an important** step in carbohydrate digestion.**
 
• However, this enzyme** is not produced in the salivary glands and thus is not found in saliva.**
 
• Rather, it's** secreted by the cells lining the small intestine (specifically, the cells on the walls of the villi).**
 
• Therefore, **maltase plays its role in the later stages of digestion, after food has been swallowed**

***Hence statement A is incorrect.***

 
• **Amylase **is **present in the saliva and helps change starches into sugars.**
 
• Amylase is an** enzyme that is indeed produced by the salivary glands and is thus present in saliva.**
 
• Its role is to **begin the process of digestion in the mouth by breaking down starch, which is a complex carbohydrate, into simpler sugars like maltose.**
 
• So when you start to chew food, the **amylase **in your saliva is **already starting to break down the starches present.**
 
• The process then** continues in the small intestine where other enzymes (like maltase) take over.**

*Hence statement B is correct.*

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of nitrate ion (NO₃^-), chloride ion (CI⁻), bromide ion (Br⁻) and iodide ion (I⁻) as per their basic strength?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is NO3- > Cl- > Br- > I-.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-), and iodide (I-) ions are all halide ions and belong to the same group in the periodic table (Group 17, the Halogens).
 
• As you move down the group, atoms will increase in size and contain more electron shells, causing the valence (outermost) electrons to be less tightly held due to an increase in the shielding effect and a larger atomic radius, which leads to these ions being less attracted to hydrogen ions (H⁺), hence less basic.
 
• On the other hand, the nitrate ion (NO₃⁻) is less atomically extensive and is what we call a** "hard ion" due to its smaller size and higher charge density.**
 
• It features oxygen, which is more electronegative. The nitrate ion is also stabilized by resonance – the ability of the negative charge to be delocalized over several atoms reduces the reactivity of the ion (in terms of accepting a proton).
 
• **However, because of the smaller size, hard ions tend to form stronger bonds with H+ ions, so they are better bases than large, soft ions.**
 
• Therefore, even though NO₃⁻ is a stable ion due to resonance, it is still harder and smaller compared with the larger halide ions, making it more basic. Hence the order of basicity, from strongest to weakest, is: NO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > Br⁻ > I⁻.

questions.question: Which element in the modern periodic table has the same number of valence electrons as that of caesium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** is the correct answer because it shares the **same number of valence electrons as Caesium.**
 
• Both Potassium (K) and Caesium (Cs) belong to** Group 1 of the Periodic **Table, also known as **alkali metals.**
 
• Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have the same number of valence electrons - in this case, **one.**
 
• The number of **valence electrons remains constant** when moving vertically down a group in the Periodic Table.
 
• Valence electrons are crucial as they determine how an atom will bond with other atoms. **Both K and Cs, being alkali metals,** are highly reactive and tend to donate their one valence electron during chemical reactions.
 
• This is why the characteristics and chemical behaviour of K and Cs are quite similar. They both form +1 ions and have similar properties owing to the **same valence electron.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminium:**

 
 
• **Aluminium (Al) **belongs to **Group 13** of the Periodic Table.
 
• It has three valence electrons, which affects its** reactivity and oxidation states.**
 
• In chemical reactions, Aluminium often loses these electrons, resulting in a **+3 ion**, unlike Cs and K which forms **+1 ions.**
 
• Despite its difference in reactivity from Cs and K, Aluminium is widely used due to its **lightweight and resistance to corrosion.**
 
 
 
• **Barium:**
 
 
• **Barium (Ba)** is part of **Group 2**, also known as the **alkaline earth metals.**
 
• Unlike Cs and K which have a single valence electron, Barium has** two valence electrons.**
 
• This difference in the number of valence electrons makes it form **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Barium compounds show a unique property in that they are very heavy, making them useful for **blocking X-ray and radiation emission**, as in Barium meal used in **radiography.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium:**
 
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** is also a member of **Group 2**, just like Barium.
 
• It has two valence electrons and hence, forms **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Its chemical behaviour, influenced by the number of valence electrons, is thus distinct from Cs and K.
 
• Calcium is crucial for human health, particularly for the development and maintenance of bones. It's also an important component of the earth's crust; compounds such as calcium carbonate are found in rocks like limestone and marble.

• Britain, with its House of Commons and House of Lords, provided the bicameral system model that India adopted to ensure an efficient system of checks and balances in governance.
 
• The British implemented this legislating system during their rule in India, which was then included into the Indian Constitution when it was framed.
 
• The adoption of bicameralism from the British constitution** reflects India's drive to bring together the best practices from constitutions around the world** while also staying rooted to its unique values and traditions.

The correct answer is __**e-banking.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net banking**, also known as **Internet banking, online banking or e-banking**, refers to the process of conducting financial transactions through a website.
 
• **E-banking** provides users with the ability to perform various banking activities, including **checking account balances, transferring money between accounts, and paying bills, among other things**.
 
• It can be done from the comfort of one's home or while on the go, making it extremely **convenient for customers.**
 
• Additionally, many more complex transactions, such as **applying for a loan or an investment product**, can also be completed** via net banking.**
 
• Net banking is **secured with the latest technology** to prevent unauthorized access to the user's financial information.
 
• Banks typically provide a secure login process with **additional security features** such as** one-time password verification or biometric authentication.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E-transfer**

 
 
• E-transfer, often called electronic funds transfer (EFT), is a system of transferring money from one bank account to another without any paper money changing hands.
 
• It allows transactions such as automated teller machine (ATM) transactions, direct deposits, wire transfers, and online payment services like PayPal.
 
 
 
• **E-commerce**
 
 
• E-commerce refers to the buying and selling of goods or services using the internet and the transfer of money and data to execute these transactions.
 
• It includes sales of products through a company website, business-to-business (B2B) buying and selling, gathering and using demographic data through web contacts and social media, B2B electronic data interchange, and many others.
 
 
 
• **E-process**
 
 
• E-process or electronic process, in a general sense, refers to conducting processes or tasks via digital means, often through the internet or other digital platforms.
 
• It can apply to various fields, including business, science, technology, and more.
 
• However, it's not a term used with a specific or widely accepted definition, unlike the others on this list.

questions.question: Which of the following types of hackers, also known as crackers, hack to gain unauthorised access to a system and harm its operations or steal sensitive information?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black hat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black hat hackers**, also known as **crackers**, are individuals who engage in **unethical and illegal activities**.
 
• They hack to gain **unauthorized access **to a system with the intent of **causing damage, stealing sensitive information, or disrupting its operations**.
 
• Black hat hackers often have a **deep understanding of computer networks and systems.**
 
• Their activities are not only limited to gaining unauthorized access but also **manipulating the data and system configurations.**
 
• Black hat hacking can result in** substantial harm to individuals, organizations, and the public, and it is illegal and punishable by law**.
 
• The term **"black hat"** comes from old western movies, where the bad guys often wore black hats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White hat**

 
 
• White hat hackers, often referred to as ethical hackers, use their skills to improve system security.
 
• They are usually employed by organizations to conduct penetration tests and vulnerability assessments on the companies' systems to prevent potential breaches.
 
 
 
• **Red hat**
 
 
• Red hat hackers are similar to white hat hackers in that their intent is to prevent malicious hacking.
 
• However, instead of simply aiming to defend systems or fix vulnerabilities, they actively engage with black hat hackers, even attacking their systems to bring them down.
 
• This proactive (and at times aggressive) approach separates them from white hat hackers.
 
 
 
• **Grey hat**
 
 
• Grey hat hackers operate in the gray area between malicious intent (black hat) and ethical hacking (white hat).
 
• While they may not have permission to access systems like white hat hackers do, they typically alert organizations to vulnerabilities they find, giving them a chance to fix the issues before less ethical hackers can exploit them.
 
• However, some gray hat hackers may also request a fee for fixing such vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following options refers to the layout arrangement of different devices in a network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Network topology.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Network topology** refers to the** physical and logical arrangement of nodes and connections** in a network.
 
• The **nodes** include devices such as **switches, routers, and software with switch and router features**.
 
• These topologies can come in a few different forms, including **star, bus, ring, mesh, and hybrid,** each of which has different strengths and weaknesses.
 
• **Physical topology **deals with the physical design of the network, including the** devices, location and cable installation,** while** logical topology** focuses on** how data is transferred within the network**.
 
• **Network topologies** are extensively used in the **architectural design of networks**, as it lays out the route that data takes between nodes and depicts how different nodes in a network are connected to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Open systems**

 
 
• An open system is a system that has external interactions. Such systems are capable of interconnecting with other systems, exchanging data, and functioning within a networked environment.
 
• In the context of computing, an open system refers to a computing device, software or system that uses an open-source model, allowing it to interact seamlessly with other systems.
 
 
 
• **Transmission mode**
 
 
• Transmission mode, also known as the communication mode, refers to the process of sending and propagating data between two devices within a network.
 
• They can be of different types such as simplex (one-way communication), half-duplex (two-way communication, but only one at a time), and full-duplex (two-way communication simultaneously).
 
 
 
• **Closed systems**
 
 
• A closed system is a type of system where interactions only happen among the system components and not the environment outside. They are self-contained and do not rely on exchanges with the external environment to function.
 
• In terms of computer systems, a closed system can also refer to a system with proprietary standards and protocols, which restricts its ability to interact seamlessly with other systems.

questions.question: _____ means sending data or a file from your computer on the internet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uploading.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uploading** refers to the process of **sending data or a file from your computer **to a different location on the Internet.
 
• This could be to a **website, cloud storage service, email recipient, or another type of platform or server.**
 
• Common examples of uploading include **adding photos to a social media profile, submitting documents** through an online form, installing a website via FTP, or placing a video on a video-sharing site.
 
• The speed at which files upload depends on the** file size and the strength and speed **of your Internet connection.
 
• Once a file is uploaded, it can be **accessed, viewed, or downloaded** through the Internet, provided the necessary permissions are granted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deleting**

 
 
• Deleting refers to removing data or files from your system or a particular storage space on the Internet (like cloud storage or email).
 
• When a file is deleted, it is typically moved to a 'trash' or 'recycle bin' folder before it's permanently erased, allowing you a chance to restore the file if the deletion was a mistake.
 
 
 
• **Downloading**
 
 
• Downloading is the process of getting data or a file from the Internet or another system to your own computer.
 
• Examples include downloading a document from an email, saving an image from a website, or getting a software program from an official site.
 
• The downloaded files can be accessed or opened with an appropriate software application even when you're offline.
 
 
 
• **Accessing**
 
 
• Accessing in the context of computers and the Internet involves entering a system or retrieving information from it.
 
• This could refer to logging into an email account, opening a file on your computer, or visiting a website in a web browser.
 
• Accessing typically requires appropriate permissions, and may need a username, a password, or other types of authentication.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mini-DIN connector used to connect a keyboard and mouse to a PC compatible computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PS/2 port.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The PS/2 port** is a** 6-pin mini-DIN connector** used for connecting keyboards and mice to a PC-compatible computer system.
 
• Its name comes from the **IBM Personal System/2 series** of personal computers, with which it was introduced in **1987.**
 
• PS/2 ports for mouse and keyboard are usually **color-coded, green for the mouse and purple for the keyboard**, to prevent confusion.
 
• Though **USB** has largely **replaced PS/2 for keyboard and mouse interfaces**, some motherboards still come with PS/2 ports since they can offer benefits like** full n-key rollover**, which can be useful to gamers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethernet port**

 
 
• An Ethernet port, also known as a jack or socket, is an opening on network equipment that Ethernet cables plug into.
 
• These ports are often found on network devices like routers, switches, or modems and are used to connect a device to a network, typically a Local Area Network (LAN), via a wired connection.
 
 
 
• **VGA port**
 
 
• A Video Graphics Array (VGA) port is a type of video connection developed by IBM and commonly found on computers.
 
• It's used to connect the computer to a display monitor, projector, or television.
 
• It's an analog interface that carries video data as separate Red, Green, and Blue channels.
 
 
 
• **RS232 port**
 
 
• An RS232 port, sometimes called a serial port or COM port, is a type of interface that is commonly used for serial communication between devices.
 
• It was once a standard feature on personal computers for connecting peripherals like mice, keyboards, and printers, but has largely been substituted by USB.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct categorisation of volatile semiconductor memory based on the data retention capability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SRAM and DRAM.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **SRAM (Static Random-Access Memory) and DRAM (Dynamic Random-Access Memory) **are both types of **volatile memory.**
 
• SRAM** retains its data as long as power is connected**. However, the data in DRAM **begins to decay in seconds and has to be periodically refreshed.**
 
• Volatile memory refers to computer memory that requires power to maintain the stored information. Once power is interrupted, the stored data is lost.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory),** which can be further divided into SRAM and DRAM, is generally a type of volatile memory, but the term itself does not automatically signify volatility.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)**, on the other hand, is a type of **non-volatile memory.**
 
• It retains its data regardless of whether power is connected or not, and it cannot be easily rewritten or erased by normal computer operations.
 
• The primary advantage of SRAM and DRAM over other forms of memory is **their speed**.
 
• They are therefore commonly used for **primary storage and cache memory **in computing devices.

questions.question: In Windows OS, when you delete an item from any of the drives by making use of the ‘Delete’ key or even by simply right-clicking and selecting the ‘Delete’ option, the item is moved to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Recycle Bin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a special folder in Windows that **temporarily stores deleted files and folders.**
 
• When you delete an item, it is moved to the Recycle Bin rather than permanently deleted.
 
• To delete a file using File Explorer, you need to locate the file and **either press your Delete key or click Delete on the Home tab of the ribbon.** You can even **select more than one file** to delete at the same time.
 
• From the Recycle Bin, **items can be restored to their original locations** if you realize you've made a mistake or need the files/folders again. However, files bypass the Recycle Bin if they're too large or if you've specifically directed Windows to delete them permanently.
 
• The Recycle Bin is per drive, meaning each drive in your system has its own dedicated Recycle Bin. For example, if you delete a file from Drive C, it goes to the Recycle Bin of Drive C.
 
• The Recycle Bin is automatically created and managed by Windows, and **users can adjust the disk space allocated to the Recycle Bin** by right-clicking on the Recycle Bin icon and choosing "Properties".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Control Panel:**

 
 
• The Control Panel is a component of Microsoft Windows that provides the ability to view and adjust system settings and controls, such as adding hardware, adding and removing software, controlling user accounts, and changing accessibility options.
 
• From Windows 95 to Windows XP, the Control Panel is a standard interface; however, since Windows 8, a simplified Control Panel called "Settings" has been introduced and is being continually enhanced in more recent versions.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The Taskbar refers to the application bar which is by default set to the bottom of the screen in Windows operating systems.
 
• It includes the 'Start' button, the Cortana search box (in later versions), application shortcuts, and system icons, among others.
 
• The taskbar allows users to view the current status of their open applications as well as launch new ones; it also contains the system clock and notification area.
 
• The Taskbar properties allow customization like altering its location on the screen, changing its size, and determining how taskbar buttons group together.
 
 
 
• **Start menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu is a user interface element in Microsoft Windows, providing a central launching point for applications and tasks.
 
• It offers quick access to programs and system settings, documents, and files.
 
• It also contains links to network connections, printers, and your computer, as well as recent documents and help and support.
 
• The function of the Start menu has evolved since its inception in Windows 95; in Windows 10, it includes Live Tiles to the right of the menu.
